title: SailPoint Admin Domain 1 questions (1.1-1.3)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with SailPoint.

questions.stem: An auditor asks for every identity in the Finance department whose cloudLifecycleState is active. Which search query returns exactly that set?
choices: attributes.department:Finance OR attributes.cloudLifecycleState:active
attributes.department:Finance NOT attributes.cloudLifecycleState:active
attributes.department:Finance AND attributes.cloudLifecycleState:active
department=Finance && cloudLifecycleState=active
questions.answer: attributes.department:Finance AND attributes.cloudLifecycleState:active
questions.explanation: Both conditions must be true, so the field:value terms are joined with AND. OR would also return Finance identities in any state and active identities in any department.

questions.stem: A data-quality review needs identities that have no value at all in the custom identity attribute costCenter. Which query BEST finds them?
choices: attributes.costCenter:null
NOT _exists_:attributes.costCenter
attributes.costCenter:*
attributes.costCenter:"" OR attributes.costCenter:null
questions.answer: NOT _exists_:attributes.costCenter
questions.explanation: The _exists_ operator tests whether a field has a value, and NOT inverts it. attributes.costCenter:* does the opposite and matches identities that do have a value.

questions.stem: An admin wants identities whose name starts with Jon, such as Jon, Jonas and Jonathan. Which query should the admin use?
choices: name:"Jon*"
name:Jon*
name:Jon?
name:%Jon%
questions.answer: name:Jon*
questions.explanation: The * wildcard matches any number of characters after the prefix. Inside quotes the asterisk is not treated as a wildcard, and ? matches only one character.

questions.stem: A search for attributes.department:Human Resources returns many identities from other departments. What is the MOST likely fix?
choices: Put the value in quotes: attributes.department:"Human Resources"
Replace the colon with an equals sign between the field and the value
Write the department value in lowercase letters only
Add a trailing asterisk after the word Resources
questions.answer: Put the value in quotes: attributes.department:"Human Resources"
questions.explanation: Without quotes only the first word is bound to the field and the second word is searched as free text, so quotes make it an exact phrase. Lowercasing does not change how the words are grouped.

questions.stem: Security wants a list of identities created in the last seven days. Which query BEST meets the request?
choices: created:[now TO now-7d]
created:[now-7d TO now]
created:last7days
created:now-7d TO now
questions.answer: created:[now-7d TO now]
questions.explanation: Range queries use square brackets with the lower bound first, and date math such as now-7d is supported. Reversing the bounds gives an empty range.

questions.stem: How must boolean operators be written in an Identity Security Cloud search query?
choices: In lowercase, such as and, or and not
As symbols only, such as + and -
In uppercase, such as AND, OR and NOT
As SQL keywords inside a WHERE clause
questions.answer: In uppercase, such as AND, OR and NOT
questions.explanation: The query string syntax treats uppercase AND, OR and NOT as operators. Lowercase words are searched as ordinary terms.

questions.stem: An admin needs every identity that has at least one account on the source named Workday. Which query should the admin run in the Identities search?
choices: source:Workday
accounts.source==Workday
@accounts(source.name:"Workday")
@access(type:ACCOUNT Workday)
questions.answer: @accounts(source.name:"Workday")
questions.explanation: The @accounts(...) syntax searches inside each identity's nested account records, here by source name. A bare source field is not how identity documents store account sources.

questions.stem: A reviewer needs identities in either the Sales or the Marketing department, but not contractors. Which query is correct?
choices: (attributes.department:Sales OR attributes.department:Marketing) AND NOT attributes.type:contractor
attributes.department:Sales OR attributes.department:Marketing OR NOT attributes.type:contractor
attributes.department:(Sales AND Marketing) NOT attributes.type:contractor
attributes.department:Sales AND attributes.department:Marketing AND attributes.type:contractor
questions.answer: (attributes.department:Sales OR attributes.department:Marketing) AND NOT attributes.type:contractor
questions.explanation: Parentheses group the two departments so the exclusion applies to the whole set. The ungrouped OR version would also return every non-contractor in any department.

questions.stem: A compliance analyst wants a list of every entitlement that comes from the SAP source. Which search category should the analyst choose?
choices: Entitlements
Identities
Account Activities
Events
questions.answer: Entitlements
questions.explanation: Entitlement documents can be filtered by their source. The Identities category returns people, not the entitlement records themselves.

questions.stem: Which kinds of data can an admin query with Identity Security Cloud search?
choices: Only identities and the accounts they own
Only audit events from the last day
Virtual appliance logs, connector traces and cluster health data
Identities, access items, events and account activities
questions.answer: Identities, access items, events and account activities
questions.explanation: Search indexes identities, roles, access profiles, entitlements, events and account activities. VA logs are collected separately and are not search documents.

questions.stem: A manager asks for the search results in a spreadsheet for an offline review. What should the admin do?
choices: Take screenshots of each results page
Ask SailPoint Support for a database extract
Download the search results as a CSV file
Copy the values from each identity's details page
questions.answer: Download the search results as a CSV file
questions.explanation: Search results can be downloaded as a CSV report that opens in a spreadsheet. Support extracts and manual copying are slow and error-prone.

questions.stem: An admin's identity search shows names and emails, but the reviewer also needs each identity's lifecycle state in the results. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Run a separate search for every lifecycle state value and merge them
Edit the identity profile to rename the attribute
Open each identity to read the lifecycle state
Add the lifecycle state attribute as a column in the results
questions.answer: Add the lifecycle state attribute as a column in the results
questions.explanation: Result columns can be chosen so the needed attributes appear in the table and in the download. Separate searches per value work but waste time.

questions.stem: A helpdesk agent types only the word smith into the search box with no field name. What does Identity Security Cloud do?
choices: It matches the term against the default searchable fields of the documents
It rejects the query until a field name is added
It searches only the identity's email attribute
It searches only the email attribute of identities in the active lifecycle state
questions.answer: It matches the term against the default searchable fields of the documents
questions.explanation: A term with no field is a free-text search across the default fields, such as names. A field name is optional, not required.

questions.stem: An account aggregation finished a minute ago, but a new account does not yet appear in search results. What is the MOST likely explanation?
choices: Search only refreshes once every night
New accounts are never indexed until the next certification campaign generates
Aggregated accounts are excluded from search by design
The search index updates shortly after changes, so results can lag briefly
questions.answer: The search index updates shortly after changes, so results can lag briefly
questions.explanation: Search reads from an index that is refreshed after changes, so there can be a short delay. Waiting briefly and rerunning the search is the right first step.

questions.stem: An access review team needs to see which identities hold a role named Payroll Approver. Which approach BEST returns those identities?
choices: Search events for the word Payroll
Search account activities for the day the role was first created in the tenant
Search entitlements for the role's owner
Search identities for those whose access includes that role
questions.answer: Search identities for those whose access includes that role
questions.explanation: Identity documents carry their access, so an identity search filtered on the role returns the holders. Events and activities record changes, not current holdings.

questions.stem: An admin runs the same complex identity query every week and is tired of retyping it. What should the admin do?
choices: Bookmark the browser address of the results page
Save the query as a saved search
Create a role with the same criteria
Store the query text in the identity profile
questions.answer: Save the query as a saved search
questions.explanation: Saved searches store a query for reuse from the search toolbar. A role with the same criteria would grant access, which is not the goal.

questions.stem: What must exist before an admin can set up a scheduled email of search results?
choices: A saved search to subscribe to
A certification campaign for the same users
An event trigger subscription for search
A transform on the identity profile
questions.answer: A saved search to subscribe to
questions.explanation: Subscriptions are created on saved searches. Event triggers and transforms are separate features.

questions.stem: An admin realises the query in an existing saved search is wrong. How should the admin correct it?
choices: Edit the query text on the saved search details page
Change the query in the subscription settings
Ask another admin to edit it on the admin's behalf
Save the corrected query as a new saved search
questions.answer: Save the corrected query as a new saved search
questions.explanation: Only the name and description of a saved search can be edited, not its query. A new saved search, with any subscriptions recreated, is required.

questions.stem: An admin saved a useful query and a colleague who is also an admin cannot see it in the saved search list. Why?
choices: The colleague lacks the Helpdesk user level
Saved searches appear only after a nightly refresh
Saved searches are visible only to the user who created them
The query must be approved by a second admin before it is shared with others
questions.answer: Saved searches are visible only to the user who created them
questions.explanation: Saved searches belong to their creator. To share results with others, the creator can add them as subscribers to a subscription.

questions.stem: A saved search was created a month ago. When the admin runs it today, which data does it return?
choices: The results captured on the day it was saved
Current results from the search index
Only items changed since it was saved
Results from the most recent nightly backup
questions.answer: Current results from the search index
questions.explanation: A saved search stores the query, not a snapshot, so it runs against current data each time. That is why the same saved search can return different results over time.

questions.stem: Besides the query itself, what does a saved search keep that affects how its results look when it is run again?
choices: The identity profile and the transforms that produced each attribute value
The source that was aggregated last
The result columns that were displayed when it was saved
The approval scheme of each result
questions.answer: The result columns that were displayed when it was saved
questions.explanation: Running a saved search shows the columns displayed when it was saved. Identity profiles and approval schemes are unrelated to search display.

questions.stem: A script needs to list and create saved searches programmatically. Which interface should the developer use?
choices: The virtual appliance command line over an SSH session
The saved searches endpoints of the REST API
A connector rule on a source
The email template editor
questions.answer: The saved searches endpoints of the REST API
questions.explanation: Saved searches have API endpoints for listing, creating and deleting them. Connector rules and the VA command line do not manage search.

questions.stem: An auditor wants the results of a saved search emailed on the first day of every month. What should the admin configure?
choices: A certification campaign that runs monthly
An access request for the auditor with a sunset date at the end of each month
A subscription on the saved search with a monthly schedule
A monthly account aggregation on the source
questions.answer: A subscription on the saved search with a monthly schedule
questions.explanation: Subscriptions email saved search results on a daily, weekly or monthly schedule. A certification campaign asks reviewers for decisions, not a report.

questions.stem: A team lead wants a report every Monday and Thursday at 8 AM local time. Which subscription settings meet this?
choices: Choose the team's time zone, a weekly schedule, both days and 8 AM
Choose a daily schedule at 8 AM and ask the lead to ignore the emails on other days
Choose a monthly schedule with day 1 and day 4
Create a separate saved search for each of the two days
questions.answer: Choose the team's time zone, a weekly schedule, both days and 8 AM
questions.explanation: A weekly schedule lets you pick several weekdays and times, in the time zone you select. A daily schedule would send unwanted emails.

questions.stem: A security manager only wants the subscription email when the query actually finds something. How should the subscription be set?
choices: Set the schedule to monthly so that the emails arrive much less often overall
Add a second subscriber to filter results
Disable the subscription until results appear
Leave the option to send the report when no items match unchecked
questions.answer: Leave the option to send the report when no items match unchecked
questions.explanation: The subscription has an option to send the report even when nothing matches; leaving it off suppresses empty emails. Disabling the subscription stops all emails.

questions.stem: An admin creates a subscription and wants the compliance lead to receive it as well. What should the admin do?
choices: Share the saved search with the compliance lead
Forward each email manually
Give the compliance lead the Admin user level
Add the compliance lead as another subscriber
questions.answer: Add the compliance lead as another subscriber
questions.explanation: The creator is subscribed automatically and can add other subscribers. Saved searches themselves are not shared, and granting Admin is excessive.

questions.stem: A subscription option adds a detailed summary of identity and access data into the email body. Why should an admin think carefully before enabling it?
choices: Sensitive access details in email can be a security risk
It disables the scheduled delivery
It removes the link to the report
It converts the subscription into a certification campaign for the recipients
questions.answer: Sensitive access details in email can be a security risk
questions.explanation: Detailed data in an email body can leak if mail is forwarded or intercepted. Leaving it off keeps recipients going to the report link instead.

questions.stem: A recipient of a weekly search subscription leaves the company. What should the admin do?
choices: Delete the saved search and rebuild it with a new list of subscribers
Disable the identity's sources
Edit the subscription and remove the recipient
Change the schedule to monthly
questions.answer: Edit the subscription and remove the recipient
questions.explanation: Subscriptions can be edited at any time, including their subscribers. Deleting the saved search throws away working configuration.

questions.stem: A team must pause a weekly report during a freeze but keep its settings for later. What is the BEST option?
choices: Delete the subscription now and recreate it with the same settings after the freeze
Disable the subscription and enable it again later
Remove all subscribers except the creator
Change the saved search name
questions.answer: Disable the subscription and enable it again later
questions.explanation: A disabled subscription sends no emails and can be re-enabled with its settings intact. Deleting it loses the configuration.

questions.stem: An admin needs to find out who changed a source's configuration yesterday. Which search category is BEST?
choices: Entitlements
Events
Access Profiles
Roles
questions.answer: Events
questions.explanation: Events record actions such as configuration changes, with the actor and time. Entitlement and role documents show current state, not who changed a source.

questions.stem: A user says the Active Directory account requested for them last week was never created. Where should the admin look FIRST?
choices: The identity profile's attribute mappings and the transforms they use
The account activity for that request and its provisioning result
The source's correlation configuration
The role membership criteria
questions.answer: The account activity for that request and its provisioning result
questions.explanation: Account activities track each requested change and the per-account provisioning outcome, including errors. Mappings and correlation are not where a failed create is recorded.

questions.stem: What does an account activity record in Identity Security Cloud?
choices: A requested change and the provisioning results for the affected accounts
Only successful sign-ins to the tenant and the IP address of each sign-in
Only the schedule of each aggregation
The full configuration of a source
questions.answer: A requested change and the provisioning results for the affected accounts
questions.explanation: An account activity groups an action such as an access request or lifecycle change with the account changes it caused and their status. Sign-ins and source configuration are elsewhere.

questions.stem: Security wants to review failed sign-in attempts to the tenant over the past week. Which search approach fits BEST?
choices: Search entitlements for the authentication source
Search roles assigned in the past week
Search events filtered to authentication actions and the date range
Search account activities for password changes made during the past week only
questions.answer: Search events filtered to authentication actions and the date range
questions.explanation: Authentication actions are recorded as events, which can be filtered by type and time. Entitlements and roles describe access, not sign-in attempts.

questions.stem: An admin wants a weekly list of provisioning actions that failed. Which approach is BEST?
choices: Save an account activity search for failures and subscribe to it weekly
Export all identities to CSV each week and compare the two files by hand
Run a certification of all accounts each week
Enable delta aggregation on every source
questions.answer: Save an account activity search for failures and subscribe to it weekly
questions.explanation: A saved search on failed account activities with a weekly subscription delivers the list automatically. Manual comparisons and certifications do not report failures.

questions.stem: What is the main difference between searching events and searching account activities?
choices: Events show only errors; account activities show only successes
Events are kept forever; account activities are kept a day
Events cover sources only; account activities cover identities only
Events log actions across the tenant; account activities track requested account changes
questions.answer: Events log actions across the tenant; account activities track requested account changes
questions.explanation: Events are an audit log of actions, while account activities follow a change request through to each account. Neither is limited to only errors or only successes.

questions.stem: A helpdesk lead needs the status of an access request submitted for a user this morning. What should the lead check?
choices: The identity profile preview for the user and its calculated attributes
The transforms applied to the user
The virtual appliance health page
The account activity created for that access request
questions.answer: The account activity created for that access request
questions.explanation: An access request creates an account activity that shows approval and provisioning progress. Profile previews and transforms show attribute calculations.

questions.stem: An admin must deliver a weekly email of identities with no manager to the HR lead. Put the steps in order.
items: Write and run the query in Search
Choose the result columns the HR lead needs
Save the search with a clear name
Create a subscription with a weekly schedule and time zone
Add the HR lead as a subscriber and save the subscription
questions.explanation: A subscription is built on a saved search, so the query is written, shaped and saved first. The schedule and subscribers are set last when the subscription is created.

questions.stem: Match each search query to what it returns.

pairs.match: Identities whose name starts with Ann
Items created in the last 30 days
Identities with an account on the Okta source

targets_extra: Identities whose account on Okta is disabled
questions.explanation: _exists_ tests for a value, * is a wildcard, square brackets give a range and @accounts searches nested accounts. None of these queries checks an account's disabled flag.

questions.stem: An admin is planning saved searches and subscriptions. Which TWO statements are true?
choices: Saved searches are visible only to the user who created them
A saved search can have several subscriptions
The query of a saved search can be edited after saving
Subscriptions can only run once a month
Subscriptions always send email even with no results
answers: Saved searches are visible only to the user who created them
A saved search can have several subscriptions
questions.explanation: Saved searches are private to their creator and each can carry multiple subscriptions. The query itself cannot be edited, schedules can be daily, weekly or monthly, and sending empty reports is optional.

questions.stem: How does a client present its access token when calling the Identity Security Cloud REST API?
choices: As a query parameter named password on every request URL
In the Authorization header as a Bearer token
In a cookie set by the Admin UI
In the request body of every call
questions.answer: In the Authorization header as a Bearer token
questions.explanation: API calls carry the OAuth access token in the Authorization header with the Bearer scheme. Passing secrets in query strings exposes them in logs.

questions.stem: A nightly integration runs with no person present and must call the REST API. Which OAuth grant type fits BEST?
choices: Client credentials
Authorization code
Implicit
Device code
questions.answer: Client credentials
questions.explanation: Client credentials is the grant for machine-to-machine calls with no interactive user. Authorization code needs a person to sign in and approve.

questions.stem: A developer has a client ID and secret for tenant acme. Where should the developer request an access token?
choices: https://acme.identitynow.com/ui/login
https://acme.api.identitynow.com/v3/identities
https://acme.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token
https://api.sailpoint.com/acme/token
questions.answer: https://acme.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token
questions.explanation: Tokens are issued by the tenant's API host at the /oauth/token path. The /v3/identities path is a resource endpoint that needs a token already.

questions.stem: A custom web app lets employees sign in and then calls the API with their own permissions. Which OAuth grant type should it use?
choices: Client credentials
Password grant with a shared admin account
A static key embedded in the browser code
Authorization code
questions.answer: Authorization code
questions.explanation: Authorization code lets an interactive user sign in so the app acts on that user's behalf. Client credentials has no user sign-in step.

questions.stem: A script's API call returns 401 Unauthorized after it ran fine this morning. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The source the script reads from is missing a recent entitlement aggregation
The access token has expired and a new one must be requested
The tenant's search index is rebuilding
The identity profile has an unsaved change
questions.answer: The access token has expired and a new one must be requested
questions.explanation: Access tokens are short-lived, so a 401 after hours of success usually means the token expired. The script should request a fresh token.

questions.stem: An API call with a fresh, valid token returns 403 Forbidden. What does this MOST likely mean?
choices: The token was sent to the login page of a different tenant than the one that issued it
The token is valid but lacks the rights or scopes for that endpoint
The client secret has been rotated
The endpoint does not exist in this API version
questions.answer: The token is valid but lacks the rights or scopes for that endpoint
questions.explanation: 403 means the caller was authenticated but is not allowed to do the operation. An unknown endpoint returns 404 instead.

questions.stem: Where does a user create a personal access token in Identity Security Cloud?
choices: In Admin > Connections > Sources
In their own Preferences, under Personal Access Tokens
In the identity profile's mappings tab for the user's authoritative source
On the virtual appliance console
questions.answer: In their own Preferences, under Personal Access Tokens
questions.explanation: Personal access tokens are created by the user from Preferences. Sources and identity profiles hold no API credentials for users.

questions.stem: Which permissions does an API call made with a personal access token have?
choices: Full Admin rights regardless of the user level of the identity that owns it
Only read access to public data
The rights of whoever last used the token
Those of the user who owns the token, limited to its scopes
questions.answer: Those of the user who owns the token, limited to its scopes
questions.explanation: A personal access token acts as its owner, so calls get that user's rights within the scopes chosen. It never grants more than the owner has.

questions.stem: A developer creates a personal access token and closes the window before copying the secret. What should the developer do?
choices: Create a new token, because the secret is shown only once
Ask an Admin to display the secret
Open Preferences again and select the token to reveal its secret once more
Request the secret from SailPoint Support
questions.answer: Create a new token, because the secret is shown only once
questions.explanation: The secret is displayed once at creation and cannot be retrieved later. A new token is created and the unused one deleted.

questions.stem: A personal access token's secret was accidentally committed to a public repository. What should be done FIRST?
choices: Delete the token so it can no longer be used
Make the repository private
Change the owner's sign-in password
Wait for the current access token to expire on its own schedule
questions.answer: Delete the token so it can no longer be used
questions.explanation: Deleting the token revokes it at once, so the leaked secret becomes useless. Hiding the repository does not remove copies already taken.

questions.stem: How does a script use a personal access token to call the REST API?
choices: It sends the token secret directly as the Bearer token value on every API call
It signs in to the Admin UI with the token name
It uploads the token to the virtual appliance
It exchanges the token's client ID and secret for an access token
questions.answer: It exchanges the token's client ID and secret for an access token
questions.explanation: A personal access token is a client ID and secret used with the client credentials grant to get an access token. The access token, not the secret, is sent on API calls.

questions.stem: A developer needs a personal access token for a script that only reads identities. What is the BEST practice?
choices: Accept the default of all scopes so the script never fails on a new endpoint
Share one token across every script
Use an Admin colleague's token
Limit the token's scopes to what the script needs
questions.answer: Limit the token's scopes to what the script needs
questions.explanation: Least privilege applies to tokens too: narrow scopes limit damage if the token leaks. Shared or borrowed tokens break accountability.

questions.stem: A service desk team must unlock accounts, help users reset passwords and reset MFA, without changing configuration. Which user level fits BEST?
choices: Helpdesk
Admin
Source Admin
Report Admin
questions.answer: Helpdesk
questions.explanation: Helpdesk covers account unlock and enable or disable, password help and MFA reset. Admin would grant far more than needed.

questions.stem: An audit team must run certification campaigns but should not configure sources or roles. Which user level should they receive?
choices: Cert Admin
Role Admin
Source Admin
Helpdesk
questions.answer: Cert Admin
questions.explanation: Cert Admin performs all certification actions and can search and report. It does not manage sources or roles.

questions.stem: An application team should manage only the sources tied to their governance group. Which user level fits BEST?
choices: Source Admin
Admin
Source Sub-Admin
Cert Admin
questions.answer: Source Sub-Admin
questions.explanation: Source Sub-Admins work only on sources associated with governance groups they belong to. Source Admin covers every source.

questions.stem: Who can normally grant user levels to other users in Identity Security Cloud?
choices: Users with the Admin user level
Any user with the Helpdesk level
Every identity's manager
The owner of each source
questions.answer: Users with the Admin user level
questions.explanation: Generally only Admins grant or remove user levels, unless the tenant is set to also let Role Admins and Source Admins do so. Managers and source owners cannot.

questions.stem: A risk team only needs to save, subscribe to and download reports and view the admin dashboard. Which user level is the least-privilege choice?
choices: Admin
Source Admin
Cert Admin
Report Admin
questions.answer: Report Admin
questions.explanation: Report Admin gives reporting, search and dashboard viewing. Source Admin and Admin add configuration rights the team does not need.

questions.stem: An engineer with the Source Admin level is asked to build an event trigger subscription and cannot find the Event Triggers page. Why?
choices: Source Admins must first run an aggregation
Event triggers are only available through the virtual appliance
The engineer needs the Helpdesk level as well
Event triggers and workflows require the Admin user level
questions.answer: Event triggers and workflows require the Admin user level
questions.explanation: Event Triggers and Workflows are Admin-only pages. Adding Helpdesk would not grant them.

questions.stem: A company wants employees to sign in to Identity Security Cloud with their existing corporate identity provider. What should the admin configure?
choices: SAML single sign-on with the tenant as the service provider
A new delimited file source for passwords
Pass-through authentication to a delimited flat file of usernames and passwords
A personal access token for each user
questions.answer: SAML single sign-on with the tenant as the service provider
questions.explanation: With SAML SSO the corporate IdP authenticates users and the tenant trusts its assertions as the service provider. Personal access tokens are for API use.

questions.stem: In a SAML single sign-on setup with a corporate IdP, what role does Identity Security Cloud play?
choices: Identity provider
Certificate authority
Service provider
Directory server
questions.answer: Service provider
questions.explanation: The tenant relies on the corporate IdP's assertion, which makes it the service provider. The IdP is the system that authenticates the user.

questions.stem: While setting up SAML SSO, which details does the tenant need from the corporate identity provider?
choices: The IdP's entity ID, sign-in URL and signing certificate
The IdP's database administrator password and its backup encryption key
A list of every user's password hash
The IdP's virtual appliance keys
questions.answer: The IdP's entity ID, sign-in URL and signing certificate
questions.explanation: The service provider needs to know where to send users and how to verify signed assertions. Password hashes and database credentials are never shared.

questions.stem: A user visits the tenant URL and is redirected to the corporate IdP to sign in, then sent back. What kind of SSO flow is this?
choices: Service provider initiated
Identity provider initiated
Pass-through authentication
Client credentials
questions.answer: Service provider initiated
questions.explanation: The flow starts at the service provider, which redirects to the IdP. IdP-initiated sign-in starts from the IdP's portal.

questions.stem: Users are authenticated by the corporate IdP, but the tenant says it cannot find a matching identity. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The identity's lifecycle state has no access profiles configured to be granted on sign-in
The source's account deletion threshold was reached
The assertion's subject value does not match the identity attribute the tenant looks up
The search index has not been refreshed
questions.answer: The assertion's subject value does not match the identity attribute the tenant looks up
questions.explanation: The tenant matches the value sent in the assertion to an identity attribute such as the username. A mismatch means authentication succeeds at the IdP but no identity is found.

questions.stem: The corporate IdP is down and an Admin must still reach the tenant to make an urgent change. What should the organisation have planned?
choices: A shared admin password emailed to the whole team so anyone can sign in during an outage
Turning off all authentication during outages
An emergency admin sign-in that bypasses the IdP, protected by MFA
A personal access token used in the browser
questions.answer: An emergency admin sign-in that bypasses the IdP, protected by MFA
questions.explanation: A break-glass path that bypasses the IdP lets admins work during an outage, and MFA still protects it. Shared passwords and disabled authentication are unsafe.

questions.stem: A company has no federation service but wants users to sign in to the tenant with their Active Directory password. Which option fits BEST?
choices: SAML SSO with the tenant as the IdP
A flat file source of user passwords
Personal access tokens issued to each user for signing in through the browser
Pass-through authentication to the Active Directory source
questions.answer: Pass-through authentication to the Active Directory source
questions.explanation: Pass-through sends the sign-in check to the directory, so users use their existing AD password. Storing passwords in a flat file is unsafe.

questions.stem: How is a pass-through sign-in checked against an on-premises directory?
choices: The tenant compares the password with a hashed copy synchronised into the cloud nightly
The virtual appliance validates the credentials against the directory
The user's browser connects directly to the domain controller
SailPoint Support approves each sign-in
questions.answer: The virtual appliance validates the credentials against the directory
questions.explanation: The VA connects to the directory to validate the credentials, so the password is not checked against a cloud copy. The browser never talks to the directory directly.

questions.stem: Users who sign in with pass-through authentication suddenly cannot sign in, while SSO users are fine. What should the admin check FIRST?
choices: The search subscription schedules
The health of the virtual appliances that serve the directory source
The role membership criteria
The certification campaign deadlines and reminders sent to reviewers this week
questions.answer: The health of the virtual appliances that serve the directory source
questions.explanation: Pass-through depends on the VA reaching the directory, so a VA or connectivity problem blocks those sign-ins. Searches and campaigns do not affect authentication.

questions.stem: With pass-through authentication to Active Directory, which password rules apply when the user signs in?
choices: A separate password policy stored in the tenant
No rules, because pass-through skips checks
The directory's own password and lockout rules
The rules of the identity provider metadata
questions.answer: The directory's own password and lockout rules
questions.explanation: The directory checks the password, so its policy and lockout settings apply. The tenant does not keep its own copy of the password for this check.

questions.stem: An architect wants pass-through sign-ins to keep working if one virtual appliance fails. What is the BEST design?
choices: Move the directory source to a flat file
Increase the search subscription frequency so failures are reported sooner
Run more than one virtual appliance in the cluster
Give every user the Helpdesk level
questions.answer: Run more than one virtual appliance in the cluster
questions.explanation: Multiple VAs in a cluster provide redundancy for connections to the directory. A flat file source cannot validate passwords.

questions.stem: Which users does Identity Security Cloud require to use MFA by default?
choices: Only users who sign in after business hours
Only identities in the inactive lifecycle state who sign in from new devices
Only users created by flat file sources
Users with elevated user levels that give Admin menu access
questions.answer: Users with elevated user levels that give Admin menu access
questions.explanation: Elevated accounts, meaning user levels with access to the Admin menu, require MFA by default. Lifecycle state and source type do not decide this.

questions.stem: A new elevated user signs in for the first time. What MFA setup will the user MOST likely be asked to complete?
choices: Upload a photo ID to SailPoint Support
Register an authenticator app that generates time-based codes
Answer a verification call placed by the virtual appliance to their desk phone
Create a personal access token
questions.answer: Register an authenticator app that generates time-based codes
questions.explanation: Elevated users register a TOTP authenticator for MFA. Personal access tokens are for API use, not sign-in verification.

questions.stem: An elevated user lost the phone that holds their authenticator app. Which user level can reset the user's MFA so they can register a new device?
choices: Report Admin
Helpdesk
Cert Admin
Source Sub-Admin
questions.answer: Helpdesk
questions.explanation: Helpdesk can reset MFA for identities, as well as unlock accounts and help with passwords. Report and Cert Admins focus on reporting and campaigns.

questions.stem: Elevated users sign in through the corporate IdP. When would they MOST likely be prompted for their tenant authenticator code?
choices: On every single page they open
When they bypass the IdP, such as with an emergency admin sign-in
Only when an aggregation fails
Only when they download a search report that contains identity attribute data
questions.answer: When they bypass the IdP, such as with an emergency admin sign-in
questions.explanation: After registration, IdP sign-ins rely on the IdP, and the tenant's TOTP prompt applies when the IdP is bypassed. It is not tied to reports or aggregations.

questions.stem: Why does requiring MFA for admins matter so much in an identity governance tenant?
choices: It makes aggregation faster
It removes the need for certifications
A stolen password alone cannot open the controls that grant access everywhere
It lets admins share one account safely because every sign-in needs a second code
questions.answer: A stolen password alone cannot open the controls that grant access everywhere
questions.explanation: Admins can change access across many systems, so a second factor protects the highest-risk accounts. MFA does not replace reviews or make sharing accounts acceptable.

questions.stem: Leadership wants regular end users, not only admins, to verify with an authenticator app. Where is this requirement set?
choices: In each source's correlation settings
In the search subscription options
In the identity profile settings for those users
In the virtual appliance network settings for the cluster that serves the users
questions.answer: In the identity profile settings for those users
questions.explanation: MFA requirements for users are configured on their identity profile. Correlation and VA networking are unrelated.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order for a script that calls the REST API with a personal access token.
items: Create the personal access token and copy its client ID and secret
Store the secret in a secure vault for the script
Request an access token from the tenant's token endpoint with the client credentials grant
Call the API with the access token as a Bearer token
Request a new access token when the current one expires
questions.explanation: The token's ID and secret are created once and stored safely, then exchanged for a short-lived access token that is sent on calls. When it expires the script requests another.

questions.stem: Match each user level to the team it suits.

pairs.match: Service desk staff who unlock accounts and reset MFA
Analysts who only need reports and the dashboard
App owners who manage only their governance group's sources
Platform owners who configure workflows and security settings

targets_extra: Managers who approve access requests for their direct reports
questions.explanation: Each level is matched to its least-privilege duties. Managers approve requests without any user level, so that target has no match.

questions.stem: An admin is configuring SAML single sign-on from a corporate IdP to the tenant. Which TWO statements are correct?
choices: The tenant acts as the service provider
The IdP's signing certificate is used to verify assertions
Users' passwords are copied into the tenant
Pass-through requires the IdP's metadata
SSO lets elevated users skip registering an authenticator
answers: The tenant acts as the service provider
The IdP's signing certificate is used to verify assertions
questions.explanation: The tenant trusts signed assertions as the SP, verified with the IdP's certificate. No passwords are copied, pass-through is a separate method, and elevated users still register an authenticator.

questions.stem: An access request was approved yesterday, but the user still has no account on the target system. What should the admin review FIRST?
choices: The account activity for the request and its provisioning status
The identity profile's priority setting
The certification history for the user
The source's entitlement aggregation schedule and the time of its last run
questions.answer: The account activity for the request and its provisioning status
questions.explanation: The account activity shows whether provisioning succeeded, failed or is still pending, with any error. Priority and certification history do not explain a missing account.

questions.stem: A source with no connector uses manual provisioning. Where will pending account changes for that source appear?
choices: As manual work items assigned to the source owner
As failed events that retry every hour
As entries in the next search subscription email sent to the Admins
As new uncorrelated accounts on the source
questions.answer: As manual work items assigned to the source owner
questions.explanation: When no connector can act, provisioning creates manual tasks for a person to complete. The work stays pending until the owner marks it done.

questions.stem: The operations team wants a chat alert whenever a provisioning action to a source finishes with a failure. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Run a daily certification of all accounts
Schedule an hourly full aggregation
Subscribe to the Provisioning Completed trigger and filter for failures
Give the operations team the Admin user level so they can watch every source page
questions.answer: Subscribe to the Provisioning Completed trigger and filter for failures
questions.explanation: The Provisioning Completed trigger fires when provisioning finishes, and a subscription filter can pass on only failed results. Aggregations and certifications do not alert on failures.

questions.stem: A helpdesk agent needs the history of access changes for one user over the past month. Where should the agent look?
choices: The source's connection settings
The identity profile's mappings
The user's identity details, including its activity history
The virtual appliance's network page and the connector log for the cluster
questions.answer: The user's identity details, including its activity history
questions.explanation: An identity's details show its accounts, access and activity history, which lists changes over time. Source and VA settings are configuration, not history.

questions.stem: After an identity moves to a terminated lifecycle state, how can the admin confirm its accounts were actually disabled?
choices: Assume success, because a lifecycle state change always disables every account
Wait for the next quarterly certification
Read the identity profile's transforms
Check the account activities created by the lifecycle state change
questions.answer: Check the account activities created by the lifecycle state change
questions.explanation: The lifecycle change creates account activities whose results show each disable action. Assuming success or waiting months leaves a leaver's access unverified.

questions.stem: When does the Provisioning Completed event trigger fire?
choices: Only when a source is first created and its connection test passes for the first time
Only after a successful aggregation
After a provisioning action completes, whether it succeeded or failed
Before any approval is collected
questions.answer: After a provisioning action completes, whether it succeeded or failed
questions.explanation: It fires when provisioning finishes and the payload includes the result for each account request. That is why subscribers can filter on failures.

questions.stem: The facilities system must be told whenever a new identity appears in the tenant so it can print a badge. Which trigger fits BEST?
choices: Identity Attributes Changed
Account Aggregation Completed
Source Created
Identity Created
questions.answer: Identity Created
questions.explanation: Identity Created fires when a new identity is created, which is exactly the badge event. Attribute changes fire for existing identities.

questions.stem: A downstream payroll app must be notified when an existing identity's department changes. Which trigger should the admin use?
choices: Identity Attributes Changed
Identity Created
Provisioning Completed
Identity Deleted
questions.answer: Identity Attributes Changed
questions.explanation: Identity Attributes Changed fires when attributes of an existing identity change and lists what changed. Identity Created only fires once at creation.

questions.stem: An external risk engine must approve or deny access requests before the normal approval process starts. Which kind of trigger supports this?
choices: A fire-and-forget trigger such as Identity Created that sends the request details
A search subscription on access requests
A request-response trigger such as Access Request Pre-Approval
A scheduled certification campaign
questions.answer: A request-response trigger such as Access Request Pre-Approval
questions.explanation: Request-response triggers wait for the subscriber's answer, and pre-approval lets an outside system decide early. Fire-and-forget triggers cannot change the outcome.

questions.stem: After every account aggregation from the HR source, a data-quality script must check the results. Which trigger fits BEST?
choices: Identity Created
Provisioning Completed
Account Aggregation Completed
Access Request Submitted
questions.answer: Account Aggregation Completed
questions.explanation: Account Aggregation Completed fires when an aggregation finishes and reports its statistics. Provisioning Completed relates to writes to sources, not reads.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a fire-and-forget trigger and a request-response trigger?
choices: Only fire-and-forget triggers can deliver their payloads to an HTTP endpoint
Only request-response can be filtered
Fire-and-forget triggers run only once a day
Only request-response waits for the subscriber's reply to continue
questions.answer: Only request-response waits for the subscriber's reply to continue
questions.explanation: Fire-and-forget sends the event and moves on, while request-response expects an answer that affects processing. Both can use filters and HTTP subscriptions.

questions.stem: The infrastructure team wants an alert when a virtual appliance cluster becomes unhealthy. Which approach is BEST?
choices: Search identities for the cluster's name
Subscribe to the VA cluster status change trigger
Run a certification on the VA's source
Subscribe to the Identity Created trigger and watch for appliance identities
questions.answer: Subscribe to the VA cluster status change trigger
questions.explanation: A trigger exists for VA cluster status changes, so the team is alerted when health changes. Identity searches and certifications do not track VA health.

questions.stem: An admin wants event payloads delivered to the company's own web service endpoint. Which subscription type should the admin choose?
choices: Workflow
Search subscription
HTTP
Email template
questions.answer: HTTP
questions.explanation: An HTTP subscription posts the event to a URL you provide. A workflow subscription runs logic inside the tenant instead.

questions.stem: A subscription to Identity Attributes Changed should only fire for identities in the Sales department. What should the admin configure?
choices: A separate tenant for the Sales department with its own copy of the trigger
A role for Sales with membership criteria
A daily schedule on the trigger
A filter on the subscription that matches the department value
questions.answer: A filter on the subscription that matches the department value
questions.explanation: Subscription filters, written as JSONPath expressions, pass only events whose payload matches. Roles and schedules do not filter trigger delivery.

questions.stem: Before going live, an admin wants to confirm that an endpoint receives and parses a trigger payload. What should the admin do?
choices: Wait for a real event in production
Send a test invocation to the subscription
Delete and recreate the trigger
Run a full aggregation on every source so that real events are generated
questions.answer: Send a test invocation to the subscription
questions.explanation: A test invocation sends a sample payload to the subscriber without waiting for a real event. Waiting for production events risks bad data.

questions.stem: The receiving web service requires a credential with every call. How should the HTTP subscription be set up?
choices: Include the password in the trigger filter
Disable authentication on the web service
Store the service password in an identity attribute that the trigger payload includes
Configure the subscription's authentication, such as basic or bearer token
questions.answer: Configure the subscription's authentication, such as basic or bearer token
questions.explanation: HTTP subscriptions support an authentication setting so calls carry credentials. Turning off the service's authentication exposes it.

questions.stem: An admin wants to react to an event with low-code logic inside the tenant rather than building an external service. What is the BEST choice?
choices: An HTTP subscription to a new web server that hosts the custom logic
A workflow that starts from the event trigger
A search subscription on events
A connector rule on the source
questions.answer: A workflow that starts from the event trigger
questions.explanation: Workflows can use an event trigger as their start and run actions inside the tenant. An HTTP subscription needs an external service.

questions.stem: The endpoint behind a subscription is down for maintenance this weekend. What should the admin do with the subscription?
choices: Delete the trigger permanently
Disable it until the endpoint is back
Change it to a request-response trigger
Remove its filter so more events are sent
questions.answer: Disable it until the endpoint is back
questions.explanation: Disabling stops delivery while keeping the configuration for later. Removing the filter would send even more events to a down endpoint.

questions.stem: What does every Identity Security Cloud workflow start with?
choices: A trigger
An end step
A loop operator
A Send Email action
questions.answer: A trigger
questions.explanation: A workflow begins with a trigger, such as an event, a schedule or an external call. End steps finish a path rather than start it.

questions.stem: Which component marks the point where a workflow path finishes, either successfully or with a failure?
choices: Trigger
Compare Strings operator
Get Identity action
End step
questions.answer: End step
questions.explanation: An end step closes a path and records success or failure. Compare Strings branches the flow but does not end it.

questions.stem: A workflow should email the manager only if the new department is Finance. Which component handles that decision?
choices: An action such as Send Email
An operator such as Compare Strings
A trigger such as Identity Created
An end step
questions.answer: An operator such as Compare Strings
questions.explanation: Operators evaluate conditions and branch the flow. The Send Email action does the sending once the branch is chosen.

questions.stem: In a workflow, which component does work such as sending an email, getting an identity or managing accounts?
choices: An action
An operator
A trigger
A filter
questions.answer: An action
questions.explanation: Actions perform tasks. Operators make decisions or control flow, and triggers start the workflow.

questions.stem: An action needs the ID of the identity from the event that started the workflow. How is this value referenced?
choices: By typing the identity's name into every step of the workflow by hand
With a JSONPath variable such as $.trigger.identity.id
With a SQL query against the tenant
By reading it from the virtual appliance log
questions.answer: With a JSONPath variable such as $.trigger.identity.id
questions.explanation: Workflow steps read data from earlier steps and the trigger with JSONPath expressions. Hard-coded names would only work for one person.

questions.stem: A leaver workflow must pause for three days before disabling remaining accounts. Which component provides the pause?
choices: The Compare Numbers operator
The Send Email action
The Wait operator
The end step
questions.answer: The Wait operator
questions.explanation: The Wait operator delays the workflow for a time period or until a date. Compare Numbers only evaluates a condition.

questions.stem: An admin saved a new workflow, but it never runs when the event occurs. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The trigger has no end step after it
The admin lacks the Helpdesk level
The workflow has not been enabled
Workflows only run after a backup
questions.answer: The workflow has not been enabled
questions.explanation: A workflow must be enabled before its trigger starts executions. Saved but disabled workflows do nothing.

questions.stem: A workflow execution failed overnight. Where should the admin look to see which step failed and why?
choices: The source's correlation configuration and its last aggregation report
The identity's access profiles
The search subscription email
The workflow's execution history and step details
questions.answer: The workflow's execution history and step details
questions.explanation: Execution history shows each step's input, output and errors. Correlation and access profiles are unrelated to workflow runs.

questions.stem: An admin wants to try a new workflow without waiting for a real identity to change. What should the admin do?
choices: Change a real executive's department in HR and wait for the next aggregation
Test the workflow with sample trigger input
Turn off all other workflows
Clone the tenant first
questions.answer: Test the workflow with sample trigger input
questions.explanation: Testing with sample input runs the workflow on demand so logic can be checked safely. Changing real data to test is risky.

questions.stem: A ticketing system must start a workflow by calling it. Which trigger type and setup does this require?
choices: An external trigger with an OAuth client for the caller
An event trigger for Identity Created that the ticketing system subscribes to
A scheduled trigger at midnight
A search subscription on tickets
questions.answer: An external trigger with an OAuth client for the caller
questions.explanation: External triggers are invoked through an API call that is authenticated with a client created for the workflow. Event and scheduled triggers cannot be called by another system.

questions.stem: A workflow gets a list of identities and must send each one an email. Which operator should process the list?
choices: Loop
Wait
Compare Booleans
End step
questions.answer: Loop
questions.explanation: The Loop operator runs its steps once for each item in a list. Wait only pauses.

questions.stem: A workflow must post data to an external system's REST API in the middle of its logic. Which action should be used?
choices: HTTP Request
Send Email
Get Identity
Manage Accounts
questions.answer: HTTP Request
questions.explanation: The HTTP Request action calls an outside API from within the workflow. Manage Accounts acts on accounts in sources, not arbitrary endpoints.

questions.stem: What is Configuration Hub mainly used for?
choices: Monitoring virtual appliance CPU, memory and disk use across all clusters
Backing up, restoring and migrating tenant configuration objects
Approving access requests in bulk
Writing transforms in a code editor
questions.answer: Backing up, restoring and migrating tenant configuration objects
questions.explanation: Configuration Hub manages configuration through backups, drafts and deploys, including moves between tenants. VA health and approvals live elsewhere.

questions.stem: An admin is about to change several identity profiles and transforms. What should the admin do FIRST to make rollback possible?
choices: Download a search CSV of all identities and their current attribute values
Disable every source
Create a Configuration Hub backup of those object types
Run a certification of all admins
questions.answer: Create a Configuration Hub backup of those object types
questions.explanation: A manual backup captures the configuration as it is now, so it can be restored if the change goes wrong. A CSV of identities is data, not configuration.

questions.stem: A bad change was deployed and the admin wants configuration back as it was in last week's backup. Which sequence is correct?
choices: Delete the live objects and wait for the next automated weekly backup to restore them
Upload the backup to a virtual appliance
Restore the backup directly with no draft
Create a draft from the backup, review it, then deploy it
questions.answer: Create a draft from the backup, review it, then deploy it
questions.explanation: Restoring means creating a draft that compares the backup with the live tenant, optionally editing it, then deploying it. Deleting live objects first causes an outage.

questions.stem: After restoring sources from a Configuration Hub backup, a source fails to connect. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: Backups only keep the source's name
Restores always disable the source
Backups are encrypted with a tenant key that expires and blocks the restored connection
Secrets and credentials are not backed up and must be re-entered
questions.answer: Secrets and credentials are not backed up and must be re-entered
questions.explanation: Configuration Hub does not back up secrets or credentials, so source passwords must be entered again. The rest of the source configuration is restored.

questions.stem: Configuration tested in a sandbox tenant must be moved to production, where some values differ. Which feature helps replace those values during the move?
choices: Object mapping in Configuration Hub
Search subscriptions
Identity Attributes Changed triggers
Account correlation
questions.answer: Object mapping in Configuration Hub
questions.explanation: Object mappings substitute tenant-specific values when a draft is created for the target tenant. Correlation links accounts to identities and has nothing to do with migration.

questions.stem: Besides manual backups, how else is a production tenant's configuration backed up?
choices: Only through daily email of search results
SailPoint takes automated weekly backups that it manages
By the virtual appliance every hour
It is not backed up at all, so manual backups are the only copy that exists
questions.answer: SailPoint takes automated weekly backups that it manages
questions.explanation: Automated weekly backups appear as created by the system and their retention is managed by SailPoint. Admins can also schedule their own recurring backups.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to build a workflow that emails a manager when an identity changes department.
items: Choose the Identity Attributes Changed trigger
Add a Compare Strings operator that checks the changed attribute is department
Add a Get Identity action to fetch the manager
Add a Send Email action to the manager
Add an end step, test with sample input and enable the workflow
questions.explanation: A workflow starts with a trigger, branches with an operator, gathers data and acts with actions, and finishes with an end step. Testing and enabling come last.

questions.stem: Match each event trigger to the use case it BEST fits.

pairs.match: Order a badge for every new identity
Tell payroll when a department changes
Check data quality after each HR load
Alert when an account change to a source fails
Let a risk engine approve or deny a request early

targets_extra: Email a weekly list of identities without managers
questions.explanation: Each trigger matches the event it reports. A weekly emailed list is a search subscription, not an event trigger.

questions.stem: An admin is planning to use Configuration Hub. Which TWO statements are true?
choices: Secrets and credentials are not included in backups
Restoring is done by creating and deploying a draft
Backups also copy all identity and account data
Only one manual backup can exist at a time
Deploys skip any comparison with the live tenant
answers: Secrets and credentials are not included in backups
Restoring is done by creating and deploying a draft
questions.explanation: Credentials must be re-entered and restores go through a draft that is compared with the live tenant and deployed. Backups hold configuration objects, not identity data, and several manual backups can be kept.
